history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: 'Shri Baba Pashupati Nath Temple' (CSV row 2372) is the same shrine as seq 1100 (id pashupati-nath-temple-bareilly), Bareilly's Pashupatinath/Jagmohaneshwarnath Temple at Pashupati Vihar Colony on Pilibhit Bypass Road - five-faced Shivling, pagoda-style architecture, reservoir with fish, built 2003. The two records must be merged or one dropped. The Pashupatinath Temple of Bareilly - also called the Jagmohaneshwarnath Temple - is the newest of the seven 'Nath' Shiva temples of Bareilly ('Nath Nagri'). It was built in 2003 by a builder of the city, taking about a year to complete. Modelled on the famous Pashupatinath temple of Nepal, its sanctum houses a panchamukhi (five-faced) Shivalinga set in the middle of a pond that surrounds the main temple on all sides, with fish and ducks in abundance. The complex also includes a Bhairav temple, a replica of Mount Kailash, 108 Shivalingas for the 108 names of Shiva, planted rudraksh and sandalwood trees, and a stone brought from Rameswaram's Ramsetu that floats in water (per Wikipedia). name: Shri Baba Pashupati Nath Temple
town_description: Bareilly is a major city of western Uttar Pradesh and the historic centre of the Rohilkhand region. Revered as 'Nath Nagri', it is traditionally home to seven ancient Shiva temples named after Shiva's Naths - Alakhnath, Trivatinath, Madhinath, Dhopeshwarnath, Pashupatinath, Tapeshwarnath and Bankhandinath. It is a commercial, educational and railway hub of the region, about 250 km from Delhi.

travel.airport: Bareilly Airport (BEK), within the city; Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi, about 250 km.
travel.railway: Bareilly Junction, a major railhead, is the nearest railway station.
travel.road: Situated on the Pilibhit Bypass Road in Pashupati Vihar Colony (Bareilly 243005); easily reached by auto-rickshaw or taxi from anywhere in the city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Maha Shivratri is the peak festival.
